subject: star engulfing planet
title: What If a Star Swallowed Its Own Planet? In 2020 We Watched One Do It

scenes.text: What if a star ate one of its own planets? In 2020, astronomers watched it happen.
About 12,000 light-years away, an ageing star had swollen into a giant and was brushing against a planet the size of Jupiter.
In May 2020 a sky survey caught it flaring. Within about ten days the star was roughly a hundred times brighter.
Then it faded over about six months, wrapped in a cloud of cold dust, like ash after a fire.
Astronomers decoded the glow: a planet spiralling in, torn apart, its gas thrown outward. The proof took three years to publish.
It was a preview. In about five billion years the Sun swells the same way, and the planet on the menu is Earth.

description:
What if a star swallowed its own planet? In May 2020 astronomers caught it happening for the first time.
A sun-like star about 12,000 light-years from Earth brightened roughly a hundred-fold in about ten days and then faded over months, leaving a cloud of cool dust. In a Nature paper published in May 2023, MIT, Caltech and Harvard researchers concluded that the star had engulfed a planet about the size of Jupiter as it swelled into a red giant.
The Sun is expected to do the same in about five billion years, taking Mercury, Venus and probably Earth. What should we run through next?

first_comment: A star eating a Jupiter-sized planet, caught in the act 12,000 light-years away. Our Sun gets there in about five billion years. What would you want to see us run through next?
